# mulib-render-bvh

<!-- Generated by tools/media_inventory.py; edit CONTRACTS or section-7 scope, then --write-docs. -->

**Area:** Rendering  
**Implementation:** C11 `static inline`; no implementation switch or external ABI export  
**Status:** bounded review candidate; **not safe On1x admitted**

## Purpose and limits

AABB slab intersection and caller-stack BVH traversal.

False conflates miss and invalid traversal; builder-generated tree assumed.

Current header refinement: Builder-generated tree assumed; checked traversal distinguishes invalid/miss.

Retain existing upstream functionality and platform providers; this header is not a replacement for a complete media/editor/rendering stack.

## Units, ownership and capacities

Use builder-produced nodes/indices. indices needs one entry per scene triangle; stack needs at least the traversal's pending-node depth (node count is a conservative bound), with cap in size_t slots. Prefer hit_checked for distinct HIT/MISS/INVALID; the bool compatibility wrapper conflates miss/invalid. Visited-node checks do not prove full tree bounds.

Scene triangles/materials, traversal scratch and RNG states are caller-owned. RGB is linear-light radiance; geometry uses a consistent length unit. Validate scenes before low-level ray/integrator calls; finite normalized directions are the normal use case. Ray bounds are ray-parameter distances. No provider GPU renderer is bundled.

Capacities describe live backing storage supplied by the caller, not merely numeric metadata. Check return values before using outputs. A false result is not a universal no-mutation guarantee; low-level value helpers and bool miss/error results require the documented preconditions. Bound untrusted counts and work before calling.

## Current callable surface

Signatures extracted from this header; dependency types and complete checks are in [the source](../include/mulib-render-bvh.h). Helpers listed here are not automatically safe foreign imports.

```c
static inline mulib_render_aabb mulib_render_bvh_triangle(mulib_render_triangle t);
static inline mulib_render_aabb mulib_render_bvh_union(mulib_render_aabb a,mulib_render_aabb b);
static inline bool mulib_render_bvh_box_valid(mulib_render_aabb b);
static inline bool mulib_render_bvh_box_hit(mulib_render_aabb b,mulib_render_ray r,double lo,double hi);
static inline mulib_render_bvh_result mulib_render_bvh_hit_checked(mulib_render_scene s,const mulib_render_bvh_node *nodes,size_t nn,const size_t *indices,size_t index_count,mulib_render_ray r,double min,double max,size_t *stack,size_t cap,mulib_render_hit *out);
static inline bool mulib_render_bvh_hit(mulib_render_scene s,const mulib_render_bvh_node *nodes,size_t nn,const size_t *indices,size_t index_count,mulib_render_ray r,double min,double max,size_t *stack,size_t cap,mulib_render_hit *out);
```

## Additional source contracts

- nn, index_count, cap are element counts. Nodes/indices must originate from builder and remain immutable. Stack/out must be disjoint from inputs and each other. At most nn node visits: malformed cycles cannot hang traversal. out unchanged on MISS/INVALID; stack is scratch. Numeric tri overflow is miss. This validates visited nodes, not full tree structure or conservative bounds.
- Compatibility convenience: false conflates miss/invalid; prefer checked API.

## Validation and integration

The [shared CPU example](../examples/media-pipeline.c) illustrates a small image/audio/timebase slice; it does **not** exercise every API in this header. The [integration oracles](../tests/media-integration-test.c) and [parser boundary probes](../tests/media-parser-boundary-test.c) are representative regressions, not exhaustive coverage.

```sh
python3 tools/check_media.py
```

The runner checks the 193 original kernels plus the shared PCM helper, isolated and in aggregate C11 builds with GCC/Clang, including canonical-header composition, separate-TU wrappers, an expected missing-static-inline-export link failure, a no-`__int128` path, and ASan/UBSan regressions. It does not validate native GPU/codec/audio execution, real-world compatibility, C++ or On1x ownership/admission. Explicit foreign wrappers, independent safety review and platform integration are still required.
